description: Single Point of Failure in Outposts Infrastructure The current architecture relies on a single Outposts deployment without redundancy. If the Outposts hardware fails or becomes compromised, all local compute, storage, and networking capabilities would be impacted. An attacker could target the physical Outposts infrastructure or its management plane to cause system-wide outages. Natural disasters or hardware failures could also trigger this vulnerability.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service
cwe: CWE-3: PEAR - Technology-specific Environment Assumption
recommendation: Implement redundant Outposts deployment across multiple physical locations
recommendation: Implement comprehensive disaster recovery planning

description: Insufficient Network Segmentation in Local VPC While the CDK code shows basic subnet configurations, there's insufficient micro-segmentation and security group rules to properly isolate different components within the VPC. An attacker who compromises a single EC2 instance could potentially scan and access other resources within the VPC due to overly permissive security group rules and lack of network ACLs.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1210 - Exploitation of Remote Services
cwe: CWE-1317: Missing Security Boundary Definition
recommendation: Implement strict network segmentation using security groups and NACLs
recommendation: Deploy VPC traffic monitoring and logging

description: Inadequate Physical and Logical Security Boundaries The current implementation may not adequately protect against unauthorized physical access to Outposts hardware and lacks comprehensive security controls for the local data center environment. An attacker with physical access could tamper with Outposts hardware, potentially compromising the CloudHSM modules or gaining access to sensitive data through direct hardware manipulation.
references: recommendation: Implement comprehensive physical security controls

description: Potential Data Sovereignty Violations While the architecture includes encryption and access controls, there might be gaps in ensuring data remains within sovereign boundaries throughout its lifecycle. An attacker could potentially exploit misconfigured S3 bucket policies or IAM roles to transfer data outside of the sovereign boundary, or leverage cross-region replication if not properly restricted.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
mitreATT&CK: T1537 - Transfer Data to Cloud Account
cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
recommendation: Implement strict data residency controls
recommendation: Enhance encryption and key management

An attacker could overwhelm network resources, target Direct Connect links, or exploit bottlenecks in the Outposts infrastructure to cause service disruptions.
